rationale:
An owner opened robot-hands.com, clicked 'Tools' in the nav, and got a page with no content. The DB explains it exactly: /tools.html is status='active', in_header=true, nav_label 'Tools', pages.sections = ["hero","tool-list","call-to-action"], page_components rows = 0, build_status='needs_rebuild', deployed_at 2026-05-10 — so it has been serving an 81-day-stale artefact (17,254 bytes of which 578 chars are visible text, all nav and footer) with nothing retrying it.

THE POINT IS NOT THE PAGE, IT IS THAT NO CHECK CAN SEE IT. Three checks look like they should and each misses for a DIFFERENT reason, which is why this survived: check_empty_sections iterates FROM page_components, so an absent component set yields no rows to scan; check_sectionless_pages requires pages.sections to be NULL or [], and this page has three; check_unresolved_sections requires build_status='deployed', and this page is 'needs_rebuild'. The generalisable statement is that a COMPONENT-DRIVEN detector cannot see component ABSENCE — an empty set is not an empty section.

I did not stop at reading the SQL. I replayed check_empty_sections' predicate verbatim against the live site while the defect was present: 0 rows. Then I fired all three discovery lanes at the site (design 22:05, completeness and quality 22:06 on 2026-07-30), all 57 configured checks, and counted the work items filed against that page_id: ZERO. Detection is not merely theoretically blind here, it was measured blind.

WHY A FOURTH CHECK RATHER THAN WIDENING ONE OF THE THREE. Widening check_empty_sections means changing its FROM clause from page_components to pages with a LEFT JOIN, which inverts what that check is about and re-homes its slot-level, per-section findings. Widening either of the other two means deleting the predicate that defines it. The three remain correct for what they detect.

RELATION TO PBP-023, WHICH IS THE REAL FINDING. PBP-023 ('UpdatePageStatusAction zero-component deploy guard') refuses to stamp a zero-component page 'deployed' and sets needs_rebuild instead — it makes build_status HONEST. But deployed_at stays stamped from the last real deploy, so the page keeps serving, and nothing anywhere acts on that honest flag. PBP-023 turned a silent lie into a permanent, accurate, unrepaired state. This check is the consumer it never had. [INFERRED] that this guard is how the motivating page reached needs_rebuild — consistent with its state; the transition itself is not traced, and I am not claiming it is.

SCOPE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. Fleet-wide, 15 active pages have sections and zero components. 9 carry deployed_at — those are the ones actually serving chrome — across 5 sites, and exactly 1 of the 9 is reachable from a site nav, which is why an owner found that one and nobody found the other eight. The other 6 are build_status 'planned' or never deployed: a plan state mid-pipeline, not a defect, and sweeping them in would make the check churn against the build pipeline it shares a site with. Hence the deployed_at IS NOT NULL guard, which is the platform's own 'did this page ship / will it serve' line (queryresolve.DeployedPageEligibilitySQL, same reasoning as bugs_open/052).

DELIBERATELY NOT gated on current-plan membership. check_sectionless_pages is, because its repair borrows a same-role sibling's layout and only planned pages have a sibling to borrow. This check needs no sibling: the page's own sections array is intact, so page-build-handler builds it directly. Only 3 of the 15 measured pages were in their site's current plan, so a plan gate would have dropped six genuine live chrome-only pages.

CONTEXT THE REVIEWER SHOULD HAVE: this check will not fire on its own. Measured the same night, NO enabled scheduled_tasks row targets any of the three discovery agents, and nothing runs triage_detected_items (263 items sat at 'detected' fleet-wide, 0 at 'triaged'). So the check is inert until an agent's checks array lists it AND someone drives that agent. That is a containment property, not a reason to skip review.

plan.summary: Add a fourth discovery check, componentless_pages, for an active+deployed page that has sections planned but ZERO page_components rows — a class no existing check can see, confirmed by firing all three lanes and getting zero findings. Reuses the existing needs_content_page item type and page-build-handler rather than adding a 78th item type. Additive and inert: registered in the check registry but listed in no agent's checks array, so nothing changes behaviour until it is enabled.

edits.rationale: The detector. Predicate: status='active' AND deployed_at IS NOT NULL AND jsonb_array_length(sections)>0 AND NOT EXISTS(page_components for the page). Emits needs_content_page to page-build-handler; severity high when in_header (a visitor can click to it) else medium; item_key 'componentless_page:<page_id>' so it cannot collide with check_sectionless_pages' 'sectionless_page:' keys in idx_swi_dedup. Sets NO 'mode' key: load_existing_content_action.go:66 treats mode='recreate' as the adoption path that loads and preserves a page's existing content, and these pages have none — omitting it leaves that action a no-op and lets the normal build-from-sections path run, which is the repair wanted. SQL lives in a package-level const, not inline, purely so the test can pin the two guards (see the test edit).
edits.sketch:
const componentlessPagesQuery = `
	SELECT p.id::text, p.name, COALESCE(p.page_type,''), p.url,
	       jsonb_array_length(COALESCE(p.sections,'[]'::jsonb)),
	       COALESCE(p.build_status,''), COALESCE(p.in_header,false)
	  FROM pages p
	 WHERE p.site_id = $1
	   AND p.status = 'active'
	   -- has shipped, so it is serving something to visitors right now
	   AND p.deployed_at IS NOT NULL
	   AND jsonb_array_length(COALESCE(p.sections,'[]'::jsonb)) > 0
	   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM page_components pc WHERE pc.page_id = p.id)
	 ORDER BY p.in_header DESC, p.name`

severity, priority := "medium", 85
if pg.InHeader { severity, priority = "high", 95 }
// cap REPORTS what it dropped rather than truncating silently
if i >= componentlessMaxPerPass {
    result.Findings = append(result.Findings, map[string]interface{}{
        "check": c.Name(), "skipped": len(pages)-componentlessMaxPerPass,
        "reason": "per-pass cap; remainder emitted next pass"})
    break
}

edits.rationale: The load-bearing one is TestComponentlessPagesPredicatesArePresent, which asserts on componentlessPagesQuery directly. Both guards are one-line deletions that leave every behavioural assertion GREEN, because sqlmock returns whatever rows the test hands it regardless of the WHERE clause — the exact shape of a rule that goes inert unnoticed. I verified this test is not itself quiet: deleting 'AND p.deployed_at IS NOT NULL' makes it FAIL with 'shipped-only guard missing from query', and restoring it makes it pass. Other four: the motivating case (asserts item type, handler, high severity for in_header, page_id carried, and the ABSENCE of a mode key), severity dropping off-nav, silence on a healthy site, and the cap reporting its drop count.

Required in the SAME commit that ships the mechanism (CLAUDE.md, the 2026-07-29 ordering ruling's surviving condition 2). Status recorded honestly as 'built, NOT yet enabled in any agent' with the status-evidence naming what IS verified (5 tests, negative control, package green) and what is NOT (never run by a live discovery agent). Sits beside PBP-017 (sectionless_pages) and PBP-023 (the zero-component deploy guard) and states the relation to both, because 'this is the consumer PBP-023 never had' is the durable finding, not the check itself.

plan.risks:
SHARED ITEM TYPE — its other consumers, named rather than merely measured (per the 2026-07-29 ruling that consumers must be TOLD, not just counted): needs_content_page is already emitted by check_sectionless_pages.go:87 and check_component_standards.go:472, and consumed by page-build-handler. What changes for them: nothing about their guarantee. This adds a third EMITTER with a disjoint item_key prefix ('componentless_page:' vs 'sectionless_page:'), so idx_swi_dedup cannot conflate them, and the spec shape is a superset of what page-build-handler reads. The one behavioural difference worth their owners' attention is that my items carry NO 'mode' key, whereas both existing emitters set mode='recreate' — so page-build-handler will take its normal build-from-sections path for mine rather than load_existing_content's adoption path. That is intended and is the repair, but it means page-build-handler now receives needs_content_page items on two different internal paths.

BLAST RADIUS IF ENABLED: 9 pages across 5 sites would be queued for rebuild, and 8 of those 5 sites belong to other lanes. Contained today by two independent facts, both measured: the check is in no agent's checks array, and no scheduled task drives any discovery agent. I am NOT enabling it fleet-wide in this change. Per IMP-016 the handler must exist before enabling, and it does (page-build-handler), so enablement is a defensible next step — but it should be a separate, deliberate decision per site, not a side effect of this commit.

FALSE-POSITIVE SHAPE I CHECKED FOR: a page mid-build. Excluded by deployed_at IS NOT NULL — all 4 build_status='planned' candidates in the census had deployed_at NULL, so none survives the guard. Residual risk is a page deployed once and then deliberately emptied; I found no such case in the 9 and no mechanism that would produce one, but the check would flag it and the repair (rebuild from its own sections) would be wrong for it. It would be visible as a repeat item rather than silent.

THE POPULATION IS NOT STATIC AND I OBSERVED IT MOVE: the census was 14 pages early in the session and 15 later, the new one being a robot-hands guides page created by that evening's own handler activity. So the 9 is a measurement at a timestamp, not a fixed backlog, and a reviewer should not treat it as a bounded one-off drain.

NOT VERIFIED: the check has never run inside a live discovery agent, so the item it emits has never been claimed by page-build-handler, and I cannot yet claim the repair works end to end. That is stated in the register entry's status rather than implied away.
